witnesses.mechanism: The first matching metadata positive and mismatching metadata both retain valid object/endpoints/S256. Only the literal trailing-slash issuer mismatch ceases to refuse. The function still returns its requested issuer argument, so a downstream issuer-field check cannot substitute for the refusal witness.
witnesses.actualEvidenceToReview: Read the original assertion failure and retained literal-issuer-mismatch public facts: matchingIssuer, mismatchFailed, classification/fixed diagnostic and the two metadata request paths. Setup, fetch, object or S256 refusal is not this causal witness.
witnesses.independentPreservation: RFC9207 response iss/state validation and S256 policy are unchanged; their failures are not blanket-allowed.

witnesses.mechanism: The owned endpoint increments the effect before its first finite comment-only SSE EOF. EOF becomes NativeMcpReconnectTransient. The widened catch gate admits a first-attempt tools/call reissue, while the retained attempt===0 limit prevents unbounded reissues. The existing second response is a valid matching JSON-RPC complete result with its new wire id. No fixture or transport response is altered.
witnesses.actualEvidenceToReview: Require the actual retained ordered tools/call HTTP rows, first finite-sse-eof and later json response, differing request ids, real effects and original first failure frame. A hang, forced cleanup, setup failure or malformed second response is not replay proof.

witnesses.mechanism: This separate real EOF fixture also counts tool POSTs before its strict typed uncertainty assertions. A replay may stop this case at its earlier request-count assertion.
witnesses.actualEvidenceToReview: Use actual first frame and retained request/effect rows. The later strict typed metadata assertion must be described as masked when the request-count witness fails first.

failureClassification: Allowed identities are a finite review boundary, not predicted failure counts or preapproved outcomes. Root must classify every actual failure and first frame. Any other identity, setup, guard, endpoint, cleanup, observer, timeout, late/unhandled error or process failure is unexplained until separately reviewed; it gains no causal credit. Preserve raw first failures and masked later assertions without relabeling them as executed failures.
preservedNegatives: One reissue and exhausted reissue for tools/list
Invalid or input_required resultType cases (their received results are not the transient EOF gate)
Legacy regressions and exact modern pin refusal
restoreProtocol: Root must first admit the exact source authority/working root and actual frozen-runner baseline; these private patches provide no ownership, freeze, quality or fresh-source waiver.

Bind both target originals and all protected source/test/runner/native/compiled/halt pins before applying one operator. Keep an exclusive original record and require exact original target bytes and one match. Do not apply both operators together.

Apply only the named one-line source replacement. Require the expected post-apply full-source byte count/hash; all other selected/protected bytes, tests, compiler output and guards remain exact. Do not rebuild or compile the mutant, or claim compiled-child control sensitivity.

Run only root-admitted unchanged frozen source tests. Observe actual raw reporter identities/hooks, public fixture facts, full body/cleanup errors, first sensitive assertion, native resource closure, process exit and post-exit facts. Never introduce signals, parser shortcuts, deadline extensions or fixture adjustments to manufacture a red result.

Before restore, root must read and record the actual original failures/public evidence and masking. Do not infer every later assertion failed, do not use an assertion text match in place of a reached semantic witness and do not assert predicted aggregate pass/fail counts.

Restore only from the exclusive frozen original after checking that the target is the exact expected mutant and no other writer changed it. Guard regular-file/non-symlink identity and descriptors before overwrite; verify restored full bytes/hash and preserved protected pins.

Close the root-owned original-source rerun after each restored operator using the unchanged frozen runner and actual current test identities. Check full hooks/cleanup/process and late evidence. Retain both red and original records separately. Any restoration or original-run failure remains open.

Only after exact restoration and its completed original-source rerun may root admit the next operator. This design fabricates no future apply/restore record, count, green result, quality waiver, formal Done or release evidence.
